criteria.criterion: A new test in crates/athena-core/src/run/mod.rs uses a fake planner whose first plan breaks a deterministic plan rule (e.g. missing fails_without); run `cargo test -p athena-core`: the planner is invoked again with the finding, the critic is first called on the fixed plan labelled round 1, and no critic call precedes it.
criteria.evidence: a_mechanical_finding_is_revised_before_the_critic_and_the_critic_sees_round_1 passed. The first plan creates README.md, which exists in the base, so it breaks the real 'file to create exists' rule; plan_findings is not stubbed. The test asserts the role order [Reader, Planner, Planner, Critic, Producer, Verifier]. It asserts that the second planner prompt contains 'already exists in the base' and the first does not, that the first critic prompt contains '## Plan under review (round 1)', and that the job is Landed. Under the base code the first finding would use up round 1, so the critic's first prompt would say round 2 and the test would fail.

criteria.criterion: A test with max_rounds = 3 shows that after one mechanical revision the critic can still review in rounds 1, 2 and 3 (three critic calls) before the cap stops the job; run `cargo test -p athena-core`.
criteria.evidence: after_a_mechanical_revision_the_critic_still_reviews_in_three_rounds passed. It uses repo_with_planning(3), one bad plan and then good plans, and a critic that always says revise with a major finding. It asserts the role order [Reader, Planner, Planner, Critic, Planner, Critic, Planner, Critic], exactly 3 critic prompts naming rounds 1, 2 and 3 in order, and no Producer or Verifier call. It also asserts that the job is Failed and that the reason starts with PLANNING_STOPPED_PREFIX and contains PLANNING_CAP_REASON and 'round 3 of 3'.

criteria.criterion: A test shows a plan that still breaks a rule after two mechanical passes stops planning (job failed with the planning-stopped prefix) with that finding in the reason, and the critic is never called; run `cargo test -p athena-core`.
criteria.evidence: a_plan_that_still_breaks_a_rule_after_two_mechanical_passes_stops_without_the_critic passed. It uses max_rounds = 5 and an empty critic queue, so any critic call fails the test through an assert. It asserts that the job is Failed and that the reason starts with PLANNING_STOPPED_PREFIX, contains 'already exists in the base' and 'after 2 mechanical revisions', and does not contain PLANNING_CAP_REASON. It also asserts exactly 3 planner calls and no Critic, Producer or Verifier call.

criteria.criterion: The planning loop in crates/athena-core/src/run/planning.rs no longer ends a round on Blocker/Major plan_findings by consuming a round; the cap of two mechanical passes is a named constant or documented, and the plan_round doc comment states that only critic reviews count toward max_rounds.
criteria.evidence: Read in planning.rs. The plan_findings branch no longer calls end_round. Below the cap it returns RoundEnd::Mechanical (line 242), and plan_round's inner loop runs the round again without advancing `round` (lines 43-72). At the cap it files the plan and critique and stops (lines 248-276). Line 446 has `pub(super) const MAX_MECHANICAL_PASSES: u32 = 2;` with a doc comment. The plan_round doc (lines 16-25) says 'Only critic reviews count toward `max_rounds`'.

criteria.criterion: CHANGELOG.md has an entry describing that deterministic plan-rule findings are revised without using a planning round or a critic call, at most twice.
criteria.evidence: Under [Unreleased] > Changed, the new entry says findings from Athena's own plan rules 'now go back to the planner for an immediate revision that does not use a planning round and calls no critic, at most twice per round (`MAX_MECHANICAL_PASSES`)'. It says only critic reviews count toward max_rounds, names the 2026-10-28 cause, and describes the stop after two revisions.

summary: The change does what the request asks. In planning.rs, a Blocker or Major finding from Athena's own plan rules now returns RoundEnd::Mechanical. plan_round then asks the planner again within the same round, with no critic call. Only a critic review (RoundEnd::Revise) moves planning to the next round. MAX_MECHANICAL_PASSES = 2 is a documented constant. A plan that still breaks a rule after two passes stops planning with the PLANNING_STOPPED_PREFIX and the findings, and its plan and Athena-only critique are filed as evidence of the stop. I ran the three new tests in mod.rs (`cargo test -p athena-core mechanical`): 3 passed. They drive Athena::go with the fake driver and real plan_findings, and show four things: (1) the planner is asked again with the finding and the critic's first prompt is round 1; (2) after one mechanical revision there are three critic calls, in rounds 1, 2 and 3, ending at the cap with 'round 3 of 3'; (3) a plan that keeps breaking a rule gets exactly three planner calls and no critic call, with 'after 2 mechanical revisions' in the reason; (4) existing planning tests still pass (athena-core filter `plan`: 70 passed; CLI job_plan: 26 passed; lifecycle: 68 passed). Athena's recorded fmt, clippy and cargo test runs passed. CHANGELOG.md and the design doc describe the change accurately. There are two minor findings and one nit, none blocking. First, crates/athena-cli/tests/job_plan.rs is changed but is not on the expected deliverables list. It was planned, and the change requires it. Second, the CLI tests no longer check the shape of the Athena-only critique record that is filed when a stop follows two passes. Third (the nit), some CLI test names still describe the old behavior.
